assertions.source: χ_(2,1)(σ₁⁵) two ways at q_0: tr(σ₁⁵) of the compiled seminormal H_3 generator (char_fast._compiled_sigmas) vs the closed form q⁵ − q⁻⁵ read off the eigenvalues {q, −q⁻¹}. `base` — and hence C, C/u² and the verdict — is built from this character, so a wrong convention here silently moves every number in the probe.

description: Re-examines audit 2026-05-29 Path 1 ruling on meson Habiro c=4 under the Q_β c_k truncation-order canonical framing. Tests whether the 0.77% miss is a bounded c_3·u³ truncation error (parallel to Q_β c_3 = -2 at tier=near-match) rather than evidence c=4 is wrong.

data.verdict: **REOPENED**: the 0.77% residual on C/u² = 4.03 is consistent with a BOUNDED c_3·u³ truncation error (analog of Q_β c_3 wired at tier=near-match). The audit's binary 'ruled out' may have made the same framing error the Q_β deep audit made: treating an unmatched residual as evidence the leading c_2 = 4 is wrong, rather than as bounded higher-rung contribution.

reexam_completed.meaning: the 50 dps re-examination reached its verdict

caveats: NARRATION DRIFT (recorded, not repaired): the three verdict strings hardcode the audit's 2026-05-29 figures — "the 0.77% residual on C/u² = 4.03" — and cannot disagree with this run, which computes C/u² = 3.99391 (-0.1522% off integer 4). The header docstring and the `[Test 1 — reproduce audit's C/u² = 4.03]` label carry the same stale numbers. The verdict BRANCH is genuinely computed from c_3_required / c2_pct / c3_pct; only the prose inside each branch is fixed text.

c_2 = 4 is ASSUMED, and c_3_required is then SOLVED so that c_2·u² + c_3·u³ reproduces C exactly. c_3_required therefore has no independent route and is recorded as data, never asserted; the verdict reads its magnitude against a threshold, it does not test it.
